neighbourhoods.name: Fleet

neighbourhoods.name: Church Crookham

neighbourhoods.name: Elvetham Heath

neighbourhoods.name: Yateley
neighbourhoods.housing: Estates of 1960s to 1980s houses and bungalows, with some older village houses.

neighbourhoods.name: Blackwater and Hawley
neighbourhoods.housing: Victorian cottages and post-war and modern estates near the Surrey border.

neighbourhoods.name: Hook
neighbourhoods.housing: A village that has grown with estates of modern houses, plus older cottages.

neighbourhoods.name: Hartley Wintney

neighbourhoods.name: Odiham
neighbourhoods.housing: A historic village of timber-framed and Georgian houses, near the RAF station.

housing: Hart is a mostly suburban and rural district in north-east Hampshire, centred on Fleet, with Yateley, Blackwater, Hook and a ring of historic villages such as Hartley Wintney and Odiham. Most homes are owner-occupied detached and semi-detached houses on estates built from the 1960s onwards, including large newer developments at Elvetham Heath and on former army land at Church Crookham. Private renting is well below the regional average, and rents and prices are high, helped by fast trains to London.
checkinTips: Detached and semi-detached family houses in Fleet and Yateley: record gardens, fences, sheds, garages and the condition of driveways.
Newer homes at Elvetham Heath and the former barracks at Church Crookham: note snagging still outstanding, meter readings and parking allocations.
Timber-framed and Georgian houses in Odiham and Hartley Wintney: photograph beams, uneven floors, open fireplaces and sash windows.
Rural homes off the mains: photograph oil tank gauges, the boiler and any septic tank or private drainage.
Flats in Fleet town centre: note fob and key counts, parking, bike stores and bin store access.
tenantHelp: Tenants with disrepair, damp or safety problems in a private let can contact Hart District Council's private sector housing team, after first reporting the problem to their landlord.
